# PRD – Product Detail Page (PDP)

*Source of truth: Zimmermann Functional Requirements.xlsx, sheets "Product, Catalogue and PDP" (PRD), "Cart & Inventory" (CAI), "Payments" (PAY), "Returns and Refunds" (RRC), "Customers, Account, CRM Sync" (CRM), "Order Management" (OM). Last updated: 2026-06-19.*

---

## 1. Page Structure

- Breadcrumb navigation displayed on all PDP pages (PRD-001, confirmed)
- Style code (SKU) displayed on PDP (PRD-007, confirmed)
- Key supporting information in expandable accordions: **Details, Size & Fit, Care, Shipping & Free Returns** (region-specific content) (PRD-008, confirmed)

---

## 2. Product Data

- Product name, price, sizes, and colour swatches sourced from the **Product API** (fed from AP21, but AP21 may not be the sole source in future — do not hard-code AP21 as the only data provider). Colour swatch assets do not live in AP21 — only colour names (PRD-002, confirmed — requirement updated for clarity 05.05)
- Style code (SKU) from product data (PRD-007, confirmed)
- "Also available in" / "Only available in" colour swatches; selecting a colour updates the page content and URL (PRD-004, confirmed). Hover-to-preview swatch behaviour (colour updates on rollover without click) is a **custom build, not OOTB, and not scoped for go-live** — see Open Items (PRD-004)
- *Open: product copy ownership (description, editorial text) — Contentful vs SFCC vs AP21 is TBD (see AGENTS.md "Unresolved Dependencies")*

---

## 3. Product Badges & Tags (PRD-005 – PRD-006, confirmed)

- Products can carry one or more badges: **Campaign, Runway, Exclusive, Online Exclusive, VIC Exclusive** — badge *assignment* on applicable products is confirmed (PRD-005)
- Multiple badges per product are supported; a defined display priority/hierarchy applies when more than one badge is present
- Badge creation must not require a code deployment (PRD-005, comment: "ideally the creation of these badges would not require a code change")
- **Badges are clickable** and navigate the customer to a PLP view filtered to products in that badge category (PRD-005, confirmed — workbook updated 2026-06-19: "captured in requirement"). See also plp.md §2.6.
- *Design caveat: badges not yet present in PLP designs ("Missing badges in PLP") (PRD-005)*

---

## 4. Product States (PRD-010 – PRD-017, confirmed)

- **Coming Soon** — product is displayed on PDP before stock is added or purchase is enabled
- **Back in Soon** — product has sold out but will restock imminently (re-cut)
- **Unavailable (size-level)** — triggers the Notify Me flow for the affected size variant
- OOS sizes visually greyed out/disabled; Add to Bag is suppressed for that size variant (PRD-014)
- All product states (Coming Soon, Back in Soon, Unavailable) must comply with **Google Merchant Centre** feed rules — ineligible-state products must not surface in product feeds (PRD-017)
- Low-stock indicator at size level: displays **"LOW"** label — purely visual, does not alter CTA behaviour or block add-to-bag (PRD-012; also PRD-030 from CAI)

---

## 5. Pricing Display

- Display price in storefront currency (AUD, USD, GBP, EUR)
- Sale pricing: was/now format (PRD-003, confirmed — subject to designs). If price changes again after being put on sale, only "now" updates; "was" is retained (REG-042, confirmed)
- Tax label per storefront: GST (AU), VAT (UK/EU), Tax (US) (PAY, confirmed)
- **Duties and taxes information** displayed country-specifically on PDP (PRD-013, confirmed)
- **DDP/DDU messaging** displayed on PDP per applicable countries (PAY-059, confirmed)
- Max configurable purchase quantity enforced per customer group (PRD-011, confirmed)
- *Open: HK/ME/US Intl/EU Intl pricing display — Global-e pricing via SFCC price books is defined and REG-041 is confirmed (REG-040 retired). Sign-off of the full mechanism (PRC-34..PRC-43) is still pending; do not implement until confirmed.*

---

## 6. Availability & Add to Bag

*Buffer stock rules apply on PDP. See [cart.md](cart.md) section 5 for the full buffer stock system.*

- Per-size availability shown (ADD TO BAG / OUT OF STOCK / low-stock "LOW" indicator)
- **ADD TO BAG** shown when quantity is above buffer threshold
- **OUT OF STOCK** shown when quantity is at or below buffer threshold (back-in-stock capture presented)
- Low-stock indicator at size level — no quantity number shown — displays "LOW" label
- **Max 3 units per SKU** (same size + colour) enforced at add-to-cart (CAI-017, confirmed)
- **No soft reservation** at add-to-cart (CAI-032, confirmed)

---

## 7. Primary CTAs & Supporting Links (PRD-018 – PRD-022, confirmed)

- **Add to Bag** — primary CTA when in stock
- **Find in Boutique** — opens as a **slide-out** (not a modal) alongside Add to Bag (PRD-018)
- **Wishlist icon** — displayed alongside the primary CTA; size must be selected before wishlist save (PRD-019, PRD-020)
- Supporting links: **Unavailable** (opens slide-out notify me form), **Find My Size**, **Size Guide** (PRD-021)
- **Need Assistance** section: links to email, live chat (with availability hours caveat), and Contact Us (PRD-022). The "Contact Us" link is an external redirect to the Zendesk-hosted contact form — there is no embedded Zendesk integration in the storefront.

---

## 8. Find in Boutique (CAI-037 – CAI-042, PRD-028 – PRD-039)

The "Find in Boutique" CTA is shown on all eligible products. The feature opens as a **flyout/slide-out panel** (not a modal). All Find in Boutique requirements are now **confirmed** but carry a **Phase 2** design caveat (design not yet available — "Phase 2").

### Panel contents
- "Find in Boutique" CTA only displays for products where in-store stock checking is supported (PRD-028, confirmed — Phase 2 design)
- At top of panel: product thumbnail, product name, selected colour, and price (PRD-029, confirmed — Phase 2 design)
- **Size selector** pre-populated from the PDP selection; customer can change size within the panel (PRD-030, confirmed — Phase 2 design)
- A **real-time inventory call** to NewStore via MuleSoft is made once a size is selected; the call refreshes when the customer selects a different size (CAI-038)
- **No auto-refresh** while the panel is open; boutique stock cached with configurable TTL (CAI-042)
- **Location search field** to filter boutique results (PRD-031, confirmed — Phase 2 design)
- **"Use My Location"** option triggers browser geolocation with explicit permission; handles failure case gracefully with inline message (PRD-032, PRD-033, confirmed — Phase 2 design)
- **Maps integration** via Google Maps (via MRT API connection) for boutique directions (PRD-034, confirmed — Phase 2 design)
- Per-boutique results show: name, address, distance (if geolocation permitted), stock status (**In Stock / Low Stock – Contact Boutique to Confirm Availability / Out of Stock**), opening hours, contact details, current live open status (e.g. "OPEN – CLOSES AT 6:00PM"), map pin, and a view more button (PRD-035, confirmed). Opening hours and live open status are sourced from the **Google Business API** (with a manual override available in Business Manager) — distinct from the Google Maps integration used for the map pin and directions (TPI: Google Business API; Google Maps).
- **Get Directions** link per boutique result, opening the location in a maps application (PRD-036, confirmed)
- Configurable limit on number of boutique results displayed (PRD-039, confirmed)
- Display a clear message when no boutiques carry the selected size (CAI-041)
- **No buffer stock** applied to boutique inventory (CAI-040)
- Fully responsive across desktop, tablet, and mobile (PRD-037, confirmed)
- Enter key triggers search in the location field (PRD-038, confirmed)

---

## 9. Back-in-Stock Notifications / Stock Alert (OM-033 – OM-034, PRD-040 – PRD-049, confirmed)

Shown when product/size is OOS (Unavailable state):

- Stock alert CTA/link displayed on PDP when selected size is OOS (PRD-040)
- Opens as a slide-out with the stock alert sign-up form: product name, price, and product image thumbnail at top (PRD-041, PRD-042)
- **Multiple size selection supported** — customer selects which unavailable sizes to register for (PRD-043)
- Customer name and email captured as required fields; **pre-populated and editable for authenticated customers** (PRD-044)
- **Marketing opt-in/out checkbox** compliant with regional consent requirements, gated by Omneo consent management (PRD-045)
- Clear submission CTA to register the stock alert (PRD-046)
- Confirmation message shown within the slide-out on successful submission (PRD-047)
- Notifications sent **FIFO** to first configurable-N (default 30) customers when stock returns above buffer; if stock is still available after a configurable time window (default 30 minutes), the next batch of 30 receives the email (PRD-048)
- Stock replenishment signal flows from NewStore → MuleSoft → SFCC → email trigger (PRD-049)
- No loyalty tier prioritisation

---

## 10. Find My Size / Measmerize (PRD-050 – PRD-053)

The Measmerize widget is embedded on PDP and manages the Find My Size experience:

- Once Measmerize generates a recommendation, the system updates the CTA to display **"Recommended: Size X"** (PRD-050 — Measmerize widget manages behaviour)
- When the customer clicks "Recommended", the Measmerize widget handles navigation to the recommendation view — SFCC does not control this flow (PRD-051 removed as not applicable for SFCC)
- Whether the "Find My Size" link is shown/suppressed based on Measmerize data availability is managed by the Measmerize widget, not SFCC (PRD-052 removed as not applicable for SFCC)

---

## 11. Size Guide (PRD-053 – PRD-057, confirmed)

- Size guide opens as a **slide-out overlay** (not a modal) without navigating away from the PDP (PRD-053, confirmed)
- Size guide content is delivered via the **Measmerize overlay** (confirmed — VR/RT comment resolved 2026-06-19: "Yes is going to be a measmerize overlay"). The Contentful-managed size guide is shown as a fallback only where no Measmerize data exists for a given product.
- *SEO/LLM risk (acknowledged, not blocking): Measmerize is a third-party overlay; content rendered within it may not be indexable by search engines or LLMs. The decision to use Measmerize is made; this risk is noted for the team to monitor.*
- Size conversion tables appropriate to the selected product type (PRD-054)
- Size guide content managed as a **structured Contentful content type** per product type (Ready to Wear, Swim, Accessories, Belts, Jewellery, Men's, Denim, Hats, etc.) (PRD-055)
- **Measurement toggle: cm / inches** (PRD-056)
- Size guide content manageable without a code deployment — content managed via CMS (PRD-057, confirmed 2026-05-25)

---

## 12. EU Environmental Qualities / AGEC (PRD-009, confirmed)

- Environmental Qualities accordion rendered on EU storefronts (`/en-eu/`, `/fr-eu/`) only
- Data sourced from AP21
- **Only renders when data exists** — no placeholder or empty accordion shown

---

## 13. Content Modules

### As Seen / Seen on the Runway editorial module (PRD-023, confirmed)
- CMS-managed editorial imagery module per product or collection (per new designs, surfaced as "Seen on the Runway"). Confirmed subject to designs.

### Shop the Look (PRD-024, confirmed)
- "Shop the Look" module displayed on PDP; clicking a product navigates to its PDP
- Auto-hides if no related products are populated; excludes out-of-stock products

### Styling module (PRD-025, confirmed — requirement updated 06.05)
- Styling is part of the Shop the Look module (same thing) — treat as a Shop the Look variant, not a separate module.
- Applies to **dresses and jewellery**; must auto-hide if related content/products are not populated; must **not** display for kids, men's, or other accessories.

### You May Also Like (PRD-026, SPR-58, confirmed)
- "You May Also Like" carousel powered by SFCC Einstein; rules-based fallback at launch
- Note: design refers to this as "More Colourful x" — implement per final designs

### Recently Viewed (PRD-027, SPR-61, confirmed)
- "Recently Viewed" carousel / "See Full History"/"See All" button (design TBC) based on browsing session
- Session-based for guests; persists cross-session for logged-in customers

---

## 14. Product Imagery & Media (PRD-058 – PRD-070)

- Multiple images per product: front, back, detail, and model shots (PRD-058, confirmed)
- Thumbnail gallery navigation (PRD-059, confirmed)
- **Hover-to-zoom or click-to-expand lightbox** on primary image — desktop (PRD-060, confirmed)
- **Pinch-to-zoom and swipe-to-advance** gallery navigation — mobile and touch (PRD-061, confirmed)
- Gallery updates to display variant images when a colour swatch is selected, without a full page reload (PRD-062, confirmed)
- Images served in optimised format at appropriate resolutions per device breakpoint (PRD-063, confirmed)
- Primary hero image **priority-loaded** (may vary per product — flatlay, model, or video) (PRD-064, confirmed)
- Consistent image aspect ratio across all products (PRD-065, ready for sign off)
- Optional **video content** (runway, model movement) as a tile in the image gallery; plays inline or expands to lightbox; multiple videos supported (e.g. studio, campaign, runway) (PRD-066, ready for sign off)
- Video autoplay configurable per video instance without a code deployment (PRD-068, ready for sign off)
- Flexible image presentation per page type (configurable background colour/treatment) without asset duplication (PRD-069, ready for sign off)
- Alt text required on all product images before a product can be published (PRD-070, ready for sign off)
- *Open: Video hosting platform — Vimeo is under consideration but not confirmed. Action open to confirm the best solution for smoothest FE experience (PRD-067). Note: the Third Party Integrations sheet lists Vimeo as the media platform (embed URL stored in product data or CMS); this conflicts with PRD-067's challenging comment ("Vimeo has not been 100% confirmed") — treat as Open until the open action resolves.*

---

## 15. Non-Returnable / Final Sale Indicator (RRC-003, confirmed)

- Non-returnable / final sale indicator displayed on PDP for applicable products
- Applies to: gift cards, final sale items, and any SKU flagged non-returnable at SKU level
- Message copy is configurable

---

## 16. VIC Exclusive Tag (CAI-046, CRM-162, confirmed)

- **VIC Exclusive tag** shown on PDP for eligible customers on exclusive products
- Ineligible customers cannot reach the PDP via search or PLP — but may arrive via direct URL or private marketing URL
- Purchase on PDP restricted to the eligible customer group regardless of access method

---

## 17. Product Feeds (PRD-071, confirmed)

- Product catalogue feed provision through the existing feeds provider, **Feedonomics**. Feed supports product availability, stock positions, pricing, visibility, labels, and other metadata.
- Product feed volume is controllable at import via **job config** (07.05). OOTB product export is CSV; a non-CSV format is a **custom build**.

---

## 18. Open Items

- Product copy ownership (Contentful vs SFCC vs AP21) — TBD
- HK/ME/US Intl/EU Intl pricing display — REG-041 confirmed (REG-040 retired); full mechanism PRC-34..PRC-43 still pending sign-off
- Full product attribute list and data model from AP21 — not yet specified
- Colour swatch management and mapping — colour mapping exercise TBC (SPR-26, PRD-004)
- Swatch hover preview (colour updates on rollover without click) — custom build, not OOTB; pending decision to log as enhancement (PRD-004)
- ~~Clickable badges (PRD-005)~~ — **Resolved 2026-06-19.** Clickable badge → filtered PLP is now confirmed (see §3 and plp.md §2.6).
- ~~Size Guide content ownership + SEO/LLM (PRD-053)~~ — **Resolved 2026-06-19.** Size guide is confirmed as a Measmerize overlay with a Contentful fallback (see §11). SEO/LLM indexability risk is acknowledged but not blocking.
- Coming Soon vs separate pre-launch state (and a "removed from store" state) — to be clarified. CS comment: "It is tricky in the back end today to separate styles that are not yet launched from those that have left the store. Perhaps this means having a state for products removed from store as well." (PRD-010)
- Video hosting platform (Vimeo vs. alternative) — challenged: "Vimeo has not been 100% confirmed - there is an open action to confirm the best solution to ensure the smoothest FE experience"; IC 25.05 "open discussion for Zimmermann re Vimeo" (PRD-067)

1	# 17 — Measmerize (Find My Size / Size Guide)
2	
3	## 1. Purpose and scope
4	
5	Measmerize is the third-party sizing widget on the PDP. It powers two surfaces:
6	
7	1. **Find My Size** — takes body measurements from the customer, generates a size recommendation, and updates the CTA to display "Recommended: Size X" (PRD-050).
8	2. **Size guide overlay** — opens as a slide-out without navigating away from the PDP (PRD-053, confirmed — size guide is a Measmerize overlay).
9	
10	The PWA's job is narrow: inject the Measmerize script on PDP, place the required DOM containers, detect whether Measmerize has data for the current product, and fall back to the Contentful-managed size guide if it does not.
11	
12	In scope:
13	
14	- Script injection on PDP (once on first mount, deferred behind LCP)
15	- Placing DOM containers (`#measmerize-modal`, `#measmerize-recommendation`)
16	- Detecting data availability via custom events and showing or hiding the trigger accordingly
17	- Updating the product code via the Global Object on SPA navigation
18	- Rendering the Contentful size guide as a fallback when Measmerize has no data for the product
19	- Injecting the checkout tracking script on the order confirmation page
20	
21	Out of scope:
22	
23	- Widget configuration in the Measmerize console (Zimmermann and Measmerize own this)
24	- Size guide content — Measmerize owns it where the widget has data; Contentful owns the fallback
25	- Measurement units toggle (cm / inches) — part of the Contentful fallback size guide (PRD-056), not the Measmerize widget
26	
27	## 2. How it works
28	
29	```
30	PDP page mounts
31	        │
32	        ▼
33	PWA injects Measmerize script tag once (deferred — after LCP image)
34	  with data-brand-code, data-product-code (SFCC SKU), data-lang-code, data-country-code
35	        │
36	        ▼
37	Measmerize initialises and checks its data store for this product
38	        │
39	        ├── data exists → fires measmerize.widget.ready
40	        │       │
41	        │       ▼
42	        │   Measmerize mounts the widget in #measmerize-modal
43	        │   Customer clicks → Measmerize takes over and renders its overlay
44	        │   Recommendation generated → fires measmerize.widget.recommend
45	        │   PWA reads event.detail.defaultSize to show "Recommended: Size X"
46	        │
47	        └── no data → fires measmerize.widget.unavailable
48	                PWA shows the Contentful size guide link instead
49	                Customer clicks → PWA renders its own slide-out
50	                                  with Contentful content + cm/in toggle
51	```
52	
53	**Integration modes:** Measmerize supports two DOM integration patterns:
54	
55	- **Standard** — place `<div id="measmerize-button">` on the PDP. Measmerize renders and manages its own "Find Your Size" button inside it. Use when no pre-existing size-guide modal exists.
56	- **Modal** — the PWA provides its own CTAs (e.g. separate "Find My Size" and "Size Guide" links). When the customer opens the overlay, the PWA calls `window.measmerize.modal.mount()`, which injects the widget into `<div id="measmerize-modal">`. No `#measmerize-button` div is needed.
57	
58	Both surfaces (Find My Size and Size Guide) point to the same Measmerize widget.
59	
60	**Confirmed 2026-07-06: Modal Integration is the required path.** The PWA owns the modal/slide-out shell (width, styling, tab switching between the Measmerize widget and the Contentful size guide fallback); Measmerize is inserted into it via `window.measmerize.modal.mount()`, which injects Measmerize's HTML directly into `<div id="measmerize-modal">` (not an iframe). The `#measmerize-button` div is not used.
61	
62	**Injection pattern:** Inject the script once on first PDP mount inside a `useEffect` with an empty dependency array. Never place it inside a dynamically re-rendered container.
63	
64	**SPA navigation:** When the customer navigates to a different product (no page reload), update the product code via the Global Object:
65	
66	```js
67	window.measmerize.script.productCode = 'NEW_SKU';
68	```
69	
70	`brandCode` cannot be changed at runtime — it requires a page reload.
71	
72	**Modal re-mount:** If React re-renders the `#measmerize-modal` container, call `window.measmerize.modal.mount()` to restore the widget.
73	
74	**SSR pre-check (optional):** To avoid a flash of the wrong UI on first paint, an unauthenticated REST check can determine at SSR time whether Measmerize has data for a product:
75	
76	```
77	GET https://api.client.measmerize.com/integrations/v1/brands/{brandCode}/products/{productCode}
78	```
79	
80	Returns `200` if Measmerize has the product, `404` if not.
81	
82	**Cleanup:** Remove event listeners and the script element on full component unmount.
83	
84	### Key custom events
85	
86	Events are fired on the script element (`document.getElementById('measmerize-script')`):
87	
88	| Event                           | When it fires                                                  | Payload                                                  |
89	| ------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------- |
90	| `measmerize.script.ready`       | Script loaded with a valid brand code                          | —                                                        |
91	| `measmerize.script.unavailable` | Script loaded with an invalid brand code                       | —                                                        |
92	| `measmerize.widget.ready`       | Widget has data for this product and is about to mount         | —                                                        |
93	| `measmerize.widget.unavailable` | Widget has no data for this product — show Contentful fallback | —                                                        |
94	| `measmerize.widget.recommend`   | A recommendation was generated                                 | `event.detail.defaultSize`, `event.detail.convertedSize` |
95	| `measmerize.widget.addToCart`   | Customer clicked Add to Cart inside the widget                 | `event.detail.size`                                      |
96	
97	## 3. Credentials and script attributes
98	
99	| Credential / attribute         | Value                                                                          | Sensitivity   |
100	| ------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------- |
101	| Script URL                     | `https://client.measmerize.com/script.js`                                      | Public        |
102	| Checkout script URL            | `https://client.measmerize.com/checkout.js`                                    | Public        |
103	| `data-brand-code` (staging)    | `b38fac52-7328-45c9-9fd8-038fac4be58e` — shared across Dev / SIT / UAT / Stage | Public        |
104	| `data-brand-code` (production) | `131b0b3c-1578-4fb0-a7b9-c46cd634843d`                                         | Public        |
105	| `data-product-code`            | SFCC product SKU                                                               | Not sensitive |
106	| `data-lang-code`               | ISO 639-1 language code (e.g. `en`, `fr`) — from storefront locale             | Not sensitive |
107	| `data-country-code`            | ISO 3166-1 Alpha-2 (e.g. `AU`, `GB`) — from storefront context                 | Not sensitive |
108	
109	The script tag uses `id="measmerize-script"` and the `async` attribute. No server-side call or MRT proxy is needed; the script is CDN-served and the brand code is a public identifier. All eight storefronts use the widget — `data-lang-code` and `data-country-code` must be set from the storefront context on every PDP.
110	
111	**Checkout tracking script:** Inject `checkout.js` on the order confirmation page only, with `data-brand-code` and `data-order-code` (the SFCC order ID). This enables ML training and return-rate reporting for Measmerize. It is independent of the PDP widget script.
112	
113	**CSP domains:** Measmerize serves a brand-specific CSS bundle and JS assets from `static.client.measmerize.com` (seeing the Moncler website as their example). Both `style-src` and `script-src` in `overrides/app/ssr/contentSecurityPolicy.ts` must include this origin.
114	
115	## 4. Consent and gating
116	
117	Measmerize sets cookies in three categories:
118	
119	- **Essential** — session and recommendation matching. Cannot be disabled; always set when the script loads.
120	- **Functional / Personalisation** — stored body measurements across PDPs. Disable via `window.measmerize.cookies.disableFunctional()`.
121	- **Analytical** — Google Analytics and Measmerize custom tracking. Disable via `window.measmerize.tracking.disableAnalytics()` and `window.measmerize.tracking.disableCustom()`.
122	
123	The consent approach is an open item (§5.1): whether to load the script freely and disable non-essential tracking via the SDK when consent is denied, or to gate the entire script load behind a Didomi consent category. The implementation must be built so the gate can be switched without changing the injection logic.
124	
125	## 5. Performance
126	
127	The Measmerize script is injected after the LCP image has painted — it is never on the critical paint path. If consent-gated, it loads only after Didomi consent, pushing the load further off the critical path. The Contentful fallback size guide loads lazily as part of the slide-out component.
128	
129	## 6. Failure modes and graceful degradation
130	
131	| Failure                                                            | Behaviour                                                                                         |
132	| ------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
133	| Script fails to load (CDN outage, network block, consent declined) | Fall back silently to the Contentful size guide.                                                  |
134	| Script loads but signals no data (`measmerize.widget.unavailable`) | Show the Contentful size guide link. This is the expected path for some products.                 |

# 17 — Measmerize (Find My Size / Size Guide)

## 1. Purpose and scope

Measmerize is the third-party sizing widget on the PDP. It powers two surfaces:

1. **Find My Size** — takes body measurements from the customer, generates a size recommendation, and updates the CTA to display "Recommended: Size X" (PRD-050).
2. **Size guide overlay** — opens as a slide-out without navigating away from the PDP (PRD-053, confirmed — size guide is a Measmerize overlay).

The PWA's job is narrow: inject the Measmerize script on PDP, place the required DOM containers, detect whether Measmerize has data for the current product, and fall back to the Contentful-managed size guide if it does not.

In scope:

- Script injection on PDP (once on first mount, deferred behind LCP)
- Placing DOM containers (`#measmerize-modal`, `#measmerize-recommendation`)
- Detecting data availability via custom events and showing or hiding the trigger accordingly
- Updating the product code via the Global Object on SPA navigation
- Rendering the Contentful size guide as a fallback when Measmerize has no data for the product
- Injecting the checkout tracking script on the order confirmation page

Out of scope:

- Widget configuration in the Measmerize console (Zimmermann and Measmerize own this)
- Size guide content — Measmerize owns it where the widget has data; Contentful owns the fallback
- Measurement units toggle (cm / inches) — part of the Contentful fallback size guide (PRD-056), not the Measmerize widget

## 2. How it works

```
PDP page mounts
        │
        ▼
PWA injects Measmerize script tag once (deferred — after LCP image)
  with data-brand-code, data-product-code (SFCC SKU), data-lang-code, data-country-code
        │
        ▼
Measmerize initialises and checks its data store for this product
        │
        ├── data exists → fires measmerize.widget.ready
        │       │
        │       ▼
        │   Measmerize mounts the widget in #measmerize-modal
        │   Customer clicks → Measmerize takes over and renders its overlay
        │   Recommendation generated → fires measmerize.widget.recommend
        │   PWA reads event.detail.defaultSize to show "Recommended: Size X"
        │
        └── no data → fires measmerize.widget.unavailable
                PWA shows the Contentful size guide link instead
                Customer clicks → PWA renders its own slide-out
                                  with Contentful content + cm/in toggle
```

**Integration modes:** Measmerize supports two DOM integration patterns:

- **Standard** — place `<div id="measmerize-button">` on the PDP. Measmerize renders and manages its own "Find Your Size" button inside it. Use when no pre-existing size-guide modal exists.
- **Modal** — the PWA provides its own CTAs (e.g. separate "Find My Size" and "Size Guide" links). When the customer opens the overlay, the PWA calls `window.measmerize.modal.mount()`, which injects the widget into `<div id="measmerize-modal">`. No `#measmerize-button` div is needed.

Both surfaces (Find My Size and Size Guide) point to the same Measmerize widget.

**Confirmed 2026-07-06: Modal Integration is the required path.** The PWA owns the modal/slide-out shell (width, styling, tab switching between the Measmerize widget and the Contentful size guide fallback); Measmerize is inserted into it via `window.measmerize.modal.mount()`, which injects Measmerize's HTML directly into `<div id="measmerize-modal">` (not an iframe). The `#measmerize-button` div is not used.

**Injection pattern:** Inject the script once on first PDP mount inside a `useEffect` with an empty dependency array. Never place it inside a dynamically re-rendered container.

**SPA navigation:** When the customer navigates to a different product (no page reload), update the product code via the Global Object:

```js
window.measmerize.script.productCode = 'NEW_SKU';
```

`brandCode` cannot be changed at runtime — it requires a page reload.

**Modal re-mount:** If React re-renders the `#measmerize-modal` container, call `window.measmerize.modal.mount()` to restore the widget.

**SSR pre-check (optional):** To avoid a flash of the wrong UI on first paint, an unauthenticated REST check can determine at SSR time whether Measmerize has data for a product:

```
GET https://api.client.measmerize.com/integrations/v1/brands/{brandCode}/products/{productCode}
```

Returns `200` if Measmerize has the product, `404` if not.

**Cleanup:** Remove event listeners and the script element on full component unmount.

### Key custom events

Events are fired on the script element (`document.getElementById('measmerize-script')`):

| Event                           | When it fires                                                  | Payload                                                  |
| ------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------- |
| `measmerize.script.ready`       | Script loaded with a valid brand code                          | —                                                        |
| `measmerize.script.unavailable` | Script loaded with an invalid brand code                       | —                                                        |
| `measmerize.widget.ready`       | Widget has data for this product and is about to mount         | —                                                        |
| `measmerize.widget.unavailable` | Widget has no data for this product — show Contentful fallback | —                                                        |
| `measmerize.widget.recommend`   | A recommendation was generated                                 | `event.detail.defaultSize`, `event.detail.convertedSize` |
| `measmerize.widget.addToCart`   | Customer clicked Add to Cart inside the widget                 | `event.detail.size`                                      |

## 3. Credentials and script attributes

| Credential / attribute         | Value                                                                          | Sensitivity   |
| ------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------- |
| Script URL                     | `https://client.measmerize.com/script.js`                                      | Public        |
| Checkout script URL            | `https://client.measmerize.com/checkout.js`                                    | Public        |
| `data-brand-code` (staging)    | `b38fac52-7328-45c9-9fd8-038fac4be58e` — shared across Dev / SIT / UAT / Stage | Public        |
| `data-brand-code` (production) | `131b0b3c-1578-4fb0-a7b9-c46cd634843d`                                         | Public        |
| `data-product-code`            | SFCC product SKU                                                               | Not sensitive |
| `data-lang-code`               | ISO 639-1 language code (e.g. `en`, `fr`) — from storefront locale             | Not sensitive |
| `data-country-code`            | ISO 3166-1 Alpha-2 (e.g. `AU`, `GB`) — from storefront context                 | Not sensitive |

The script tag uses `id="measmerize-script"` and the `async` attribute. No server-side call or MRT proxy is needed; the script is CDN-served and the brand code is a public identifier. All eight storefronts use the widget — `data-lang-code` and `data-country-code` must be set from the storefront context on every PDP.

**Checkout tracking script:** Inject `checkout.js` on the order confirmation page only, with `data-brand-code` and `data-order-code` (the SFCC order ID). This enables ML training and return-rate reporting for Measmerize. It is independent of the PDP widget script.

**CSP domains:** Measmerize serves a brand-specific CSS bundle and JS assets from `static.client.measmerize.com` (seeing the Moncler website as their example). Both `style-src` and `script-src` in `overrides/app/ssr/contentSecurityPolicy.ts` must include this origin.

## 4. Consent and gating

Measmerize sets cookies in three categories:

- **Essential** — session and recommendation matching. Cannot be disabled; always set when the script loads.
- **Functional / Personalisation** — stored body measurements across PDPs. Disable via `window.measmerize.cookies.disableFunctional()`.
- **Analytical** — Google Analytics and Measmerize custom tracking. Disable via `window.measmerize.tracking.disableAnalytics()` and `window.measmerize.tracking.disableCustom()`.

The consent approach is an open item (§5.1): whether to load the script freely and disable non-essential tracking via the SDK when consent is denied, or to gate the entire script load behind a Didomi consent category. The implementation must be built so the gate can be switched without changing the injection logic.

## 5. Performance

The Measmerize script is injected after the LCP image has painted — it is never on the critical paint path. If consent-gated, it loads only after Didomi consent, pushing the load further off the critical path. The Contentful fallback size guide loads lazily as part of the slide-out component.

## 6. Failure modes and graceful degradation

| Failure                                                            | Behaviour                                                                                         |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Script fails to load (CDN outage, network block, consent declined) | Fall back silently to the Contentful size guide.                                                  |
| Script loads but signals no data (`measmerize.widget.unavailable`) | Show the Contentful size guide link. This is the expected path for some products.                 |
| Contentful size guide also unavailable                             | Hide the size guide entry point entirely. Do not show a broken overlay.                           |
| Measmerize overlay fails to open after customer click              | Show a toast: "Size guide temporarily unavailable." The purchase flow is never blocked on sizing. |

## 7. Open items requiring client confirmation

1. **Consent approach.** Zimmermann privacy / legal to confirm which of two approaches applies: (a) load the script freely and call `window.measmerize.tracking.disableAnalytics()` / `disableCustom()` / `cookies.disableFunctional()` when consent is denied (Essential cookies always run), or (b) gate the entire script load behind a Didomi consent category. This is a **blocking** decision. If approach (b) is chosen, Zimmermann Privacy to also confirm the Didomi consent category and Tell No Lies to supply the corresponding Didomi vendor / feature ID. **Owner:** Zimmermann.

26

28	
29	```
30	Browser (My Account → Appointments section)
31	        │  Customer's SLAS access token (JWT) is present after SFCC login
32	        ▼
33	PWA fetches /mobify/proxy/booxi/<endpoint>
34	   Authorization: Bearer <SLAS access token>
35	        │
36	        ▼
37	MRT Node layer:
38	   1. Validates the SLAS JWT signature against SFCC's published JWKS
39	   2. Drops the inbound Authorization header and sets the Booxi credential
40	      header instead (Booxi authenticates via its own `Booxi-PartnerKey`
41	      header, not a bearer `Authorization` header)

43	   4. Forwards to https://<booxi-host>/<endpoint>
44	        │

46	Booxi API:

52	```
53	
54	- The browser never carries the Booxi credential. The Booxi API credential is held as an MRT environment variable and is appended only on the MRT → Booxi leg.
55	- The appointments section is read-only and authenticated — it renders only for a logged-in customer on the My Account route.
56	- The section is built as a self-contained module so it can be enabled when Booxi is ready without restructuring the surrounding My Account page (CRM-167).
57

59	
60	| Credential | Where used | Sensitivity |
61	|---|---|---|
62	| Booxi Partner API key (sent in the `Booxi-PartnerKey` header) | MRT environment variable; injected by MRT before forwarding | Secret — Booxi mandates this key is used server-side only and never reaches the browser |
63	| Customer SLAS access token (JWT) | Forwarded from the browser to MRT; used by MRT to authenticate the customer | Sensitive — proves user identity |
64	| SFCC JWKS | Used by MRT to verify the SLAS JWT signature | Public |
65	
66	- **No Booxi credential in the browser bundle.** The Booxi credential is held server-side as an MRT environment variable, appended on the MRT → Booxi leg only.

The recommended approach is that MRT validates the customer's SLAS JWT and resolves the corresponding Booxi customer reference server-side (from a Booxi customer ID held on the SFCC/Omneo profile, or via a Booxi lookup), then scopes the request to that reference. 68	- One Booxi API credential per environment. Rotation cadence and named owner are tracked in §11.

71	
72	| Direction | Data | Notes |
73	|---|---|---|
74	| Browser → MRT | Customer JWT (SLAS access token); endpoint path | The browser never sees the Booxi credential and never passes a customer identifier as input. |
75	| MRT → Booxi | Booxi API credential; customer-scoped identifier resolved server-side | The credential authorises the channel; the resolved identity scopes the data. |
76	| Booxi → MRT → Browser | Typed JSON — appointment history (date/time, boutique, appointment type, status) | MRT projects only the fields the My Account section renders. |
77	
78	The customer sees only their own appointment data, which they already own. No payment data is involved on this path.
79	
80	## 6. Performance and loading strategy
81	
82	- The appointment history read fires only when the My Account appointments section is in view — it does not preload on the dashboard or any other route.
83	- TanStack Query caches the appointment history response on the client; stale data is acceptable for history display.
84	- The My Account appointments module is route-level code-split so it adds nothing to other route bundles, and so it can ship dark until Booxi is enabled (CRM-167).
85	- `<link rel="preconnect">` to the Booxi host is emitted from the My Account routes once the customer is authenticated and the section is enabled.
86	
87	## 7. Multi-region behaviour
88	
89	- Appointments are boutique-bound; the history list reflects whichever boutiques the customer has booked with, independent of the storefront locale.
90	- A single Booxi tenant is assumed across all eight storefronts; per-region boutique availability is configured in Booxi, not in the PWA.
91	- Locale affects only the display formatting of dates and labels in the storefront, not the Booxi request.
92	
93	## 8. Failure modes and graceful degradation
94	
95	Each external system must fail independently — a Booxi outage must not break the My Account page.
96	
97	| Failure | Behaviour |
98	|---|---|
99	| MRT cannot verify the SLAS JWT (expired, invalid) | Return 401 to the browser without calling Booxi. The storefront triggers a silent SLAS refresh and retries; if refresh fails, force re-login. |
100	| Booxi 5xx or timeout on the history read | Suppress the appointments section (or show a compact "appointments temporarily unavailable" state with a retry CTA) rather than throwing. The rest of My Account renders normally. Never block the page on Booxi. |
101	| Customer has no appointment history | Render an explicit empty state, not an error. |
102	| Customer is unauthenticated on the route | Standard My Account authentication redirect. No Booxi request is issued. |
103	| Booxi rotates or revokes the API credential | Rotation is handled in the MRT environment configuration by the integration team. No browser-side change required. |
104	
105	## 9. Security and privacy
106	
107	- The Booxi API credential is held as an MRT environment variable and never appears in browser JavaScript, request URLs, or logs. MRT redacts the Authorization header in its access logs.
108	- The customer's SLAS JWT is forwarded to MRT only over TLS 1.2+ and is not forwarded to Booxi as a raw identity token — MRT resolves the customer-scoped Booxi reference server-side so the browser cannot request another customer's data.
109	- No appointment identifier or customer reference is accepted from the browser as an input to the request.
110	- The browser calls the same-origin MRT proxy path (`/mobify/proxy/booxi/...`) — no CSP `connect-src` entry for Booxi's host is needed; MRT makes the server-side call to Booxi outside the browser's CSP boundary.
111	- On a right-to-erasure request (REG-060–067), removal of appointment data in Booxi is handled by the CRM/integration team through Booxi's own erasure process; the storefront has no separate erasure flow for Booxi data.
112	
113	## 10. Open items requiring client confirmation
114	
115	1. **Storefront scope (CRM-165 – CRM-167).** Confirm whether the My Account appointments surface is read-only history (current assumption) or whether in-storefront booking / rescheduling / cancellation is also in scope. Until confirmed, the section is built read-only and structured to slot in without redesign.
116	2. **Booxi API specification.** Booxi to publish the API contract for appointment history — endpoint(s), request and response schemas, the appointment status values and their customer-facing copy, error codes, and pagination. The PWA-side types are generated from this contract.
117	3. **Customer-identification mechanism (PWA-direct path).** Confirm how the storefront proves customer identity to Booxi without allowing the browser to retrieve an arbitrary customer's appointments. Confirm whether a Booxi customer ID is stored on the SFCC/Omneo profile (and how it is populated), or whether MRT must look the customer up in Booxi at request time. The mechanism must prevent impersonation.
118	4. **Per-environment Booxi credentials.** Booxi to supply, per environment: Booxi API host, API credential, and the credential rotation cadence and named owner. Note the API host is region-specific (e.g. a North America vs EU base URL), so confirm which regional host serves Zimmermann.

You're prepping backlog-refinement notes for a Salesforce PWA Kit storefront (Zimmermann) FED Lead, for Jira ticket SFCC-272 "Cart Item Remove and Wishlist Actions". Read-only research — you are not writing to Jira or Confluence.

SHARED GROUND TRUTH (cite, don't re-derive):
- Today is 2026-09-03. Real Sprint 4 runs 2026-08-24–2026-09-07 (active now); Sprint 5 runs 2026-09-07–2026-09-21. The repo's .docs/memory/sprintScope.md is CONFIRMED STALE — judge this ticket on its own Jira status/fields.
- Figma 04.7 Component Inventory (re-checked live today): "Cart Item" module status = "Not Confirmed" (PWA Kit).
- Cart PRD (.docs/prd/cart.md) §1/§2 (CAI-004, CAI-008): "Move to Wishlist is authenticated-only at launch — only logged-in customers can move a cart item to wishlist; an unauthenticated user selecting Move to Wishlist is prompted to log in first." Guest wishlist is an out-of-scope enhancement for go-live. §4/§12 (ENH-038/039): the actual wishlist hosting platform (SFCC vs Omneo) is "being sized, not confirmed" — but the login-prompt behaviour itself is explicitly independent of where the wishlist ends up living, so that part shouldn't block FE build.
- overrides/app/hooks/use-current-basket.ts is a Tier 1 frozen file (owner: Integration/SI Partner) — flag if Remove needs a basket-mutation capability not already exposed by it. There's likely also a not-yet-built wishlist-mutation hook — check overrides/app/hooks/ for anything wishlist-related and flag if none exists.
- New Zimmermann components live at overrides/app/components/ui-kits/{atoms,molecules,organisms}/<camelCase>/ — check current state.

DO THIS:
1. Fetch the full ticket: jira_get_issue(issue_key='SFCC-272', fields='summary,description,status,issuelinks,comment,attachment,parent', comment_limit=20). Read description, AC, comments, any figma.com URL.
2. Check overrides/app/hooks/ for any existing wishlist hook/utility.
3. Apply the seven-point sizing lens: (1) any FE impact? (2) is the requirement clear enough to size? (3) which surfaces does it touch? (4) design/Figma dependencies? (5) API/backend dependencies? (6) pure FE, shared FE/BE, or needs architecture input? (7) size now, or need clarification first?
4. Read for the four standing axes: behaviour (does the AC explicitly cover the guest-vs-authenticated branch for Move-to-Wishlist? this is the single most likely gap given how explicit the PRD is), desktop/mobile, a11y (confirm-before-remove pattern, focus management after removal), data — flag anything genuinely unclear.
5. Design dependency: does the design exist for both the Remove action AND the guest-login-prompt state specifically (not just the happy path)?
6. Altitude: BAs own component-decomposition questions, devs own atomic/build questions.

OUTPUT, in this exact shape:
- One-line plain-language summary
- Seven lens answers
- Four axes, flagging what's unclear
- Design status + source
- Whether the AC actually covers the guest-vs-authenticated Move-to-Wishlist branch (explicit yes/no + why)
- Specific questions to raise, each tagged with who should answer it
- One-line readiness call

Be concrete, don't editorialize past what the data supports, and say plainly what you couldn't check.

<result># SFCC-317 "Zimmermann Benefits - PWA Kit Render" — Backlog Refinement Notes

## One-line summary
A thin, Contentful-driven section (label + 3 icon/text benefit tiles, e.g. FREE RETURNS / FAST SHIPPING / SECURE PAYMENTS) that renders on the Cart, built by composing the not-yet-built Icon-and-Text PWA component (SFCC-836) rather than as a standalone component.

## Seven-point sizing lens

1. **Any FE impact?** Yes — this is explicitly a PWA Kit render story (fetch + display Contentful content). No commerce/basket logic.
2. **Is the requirement clear enough to size?** Mostly. The behavioural contract (render label + tiles, degrade silently if entry unpublished/fetch fails) is unambiguous and matches AGENTS.md's Graceful Degradation policy verbatim. What's under-specified is the *build contract*: SFCC-317 is described as "not a component build" but a composition of SFCC-836 — so its actual size depends on SFCC-836's prop API, which doesn't exist yet.
3. **Which surfaces does it touch?** Per the ticket: the user-story line says "within the cart drawer," but the description then names two states — populated cart (SFCC-825) and empty cart (SFCC-277) — both children of the Cart epic (SFCC-11), and SFCC-301 (linked from SFCC-277) is titled "Cart **Page** – Recommendation Component Slot." That's an internal inconsistency: "drawer" language vs. "page" language for what may be the same surface. No cart page or drawer component exists anywhere in the repo yet (`overrides/app/pages` has only `experience`, `home`, `my-new-route`, `product-detail`, `contentfulPreview`; no `minicart`/`cart-drawer` hits anywhere), so this can't be resolved by checking code — it's a genuine open question.
4. **Design/Figma dependencies?** Yes, and satisfied at the requirements level — see Design status below.
5. **API/backend dependencies?** Yes, entirely — content comes from SFCC-316 (Benefits content type) and transitively SFCC-835 (Icon-and-Text content type, since each Benefits tile *is* an Icon-and-Text entry). Neither schema is built; both tickets sit at **Tech design / To Do**.
6. **Pure FE, shared FE/BE, or needs architecture input?** CMS-driven FE (would file under Storybook `Contentful/` per components.md) — no Commerce Cloud/SFCC backend involvement. No architecture input needed beyond agreeing the render contract once SFCC-835/836 lock their shapes.
7. **Size now, or need clarification first?** Roughly t-shirt-sizeable now (the "Contentful story + thin PWA render story" pattern is well-established in this backlog), but a confident point estimate should wait on SFCC-836's component contract and the surface-naming ambiguity in point 3 — see readiness call.

## Four standing axes

- **Behaviour:** Clear at the section level (render tiles; if the Contentful entry is unpublished or the fetch fails, render nothing, no layout impact). **Unclear:** whether there's a *partial*-failure case — e.g. 1 of 3 tiles missing a field — and whether that's handled by SFCC-836 per-tile or bubbles up to hide the whole section. SFCC-836 says it "handles empty/error states" but that's scoped to the tile component, not stated for the section wrapper.
- **Desktop/mobile:** Both states have attached reference screenshots (desktop `image-20260817-031845.png`, mobile `image-20260828-002830.png` on SFCC-317; equivalent pair on SFCC-316). I confirmed the attachments exist (filenames, uploader, dates) but did not render/view their pixel content, so I can't independently confirm whether mobile uses SFCC-836/835's "vertical layout" variant or a horizontal 3-across squeeze — **flag as unclear**, resolvable by opening the attachments or Figma node directly.
- **A11y:** SFCC-836 commits to accessibility requirements for the tile component itself. SFCC-317 has no explicit a11y statement for the section wrapper (e.g., heading level for the section label, whether the section is a labelled landmark). **Unclear**, likely minor, but not stated.
- **Data:** Shape is inferable (section label string + list of tiles, each tile = icon + heading + optional body, per SFCC-316/835 text) but **not locked** — both source schemas are still Tech design. This is the single biggest open item.

## Design status
**A design exists.** Direct Figma link on both SFCC-316 and SFCC-317 (`Zimmermann_Design_System_2026`, node-id `40003224-108794` for the Benefits section specifically; SFCC-835/836 separately link node-id `40003038-130551` for the generic Icon-and-Text UI-kit component). Both tickets also carry desktop + mobile screenshots uploaded directly by Isabel Chaloner (designer), dated 2026-08-17 and updated 2026-08-28. This reconciles with the given ground truth that Figma 04.7's Component Inventory has no "Benefits" row — that's expected, since Benefits is a section composition of the separately-tracked Icon-and-Text atom, not its own catalogued component. I did not independently open the Figma file to confirm the node resolves — going only off ticket-cited evidence.

## Reuse vs. bespoke build
**Confirmed reuse, not an open question.** SFCC-317's own description states "Each tile is built using the Contentful Icon and Text component [SFCC-835]... This is not a component build." SFCC-835 independently lists "Zimmermann Benefits on Cart Page" as a usage example of the Icon-and-Text component. So SFCC-317's real scope is: fetch the entry → render a section label → compose N instances of SFCC-836 for the tiles → apply design-system background/spacing → degrade the whole section on failure. **Caveat:** SFCC-836 doesn't exist in the repo yet (no `iconAndText`/`icon-and-text` directory anywhere under `overrides/app/components/ui-kits`), so this is reuse of something still to be built, not something available today.

Read-only research — you are not writing to Jira or Confluence. The requester mentioned "feel like we refined this one already" — check whether that's actually true from the ticket's own history before treating this as fresh.

I've already read the full integration doc and PRD coverage for Measmerize, verified today (2026-09-03). Your job is to fetch the actual ticket, check its comment/change history for prior refinement, and fill remaining gaps — NOT to re-derive the integration detail below.

CONFIRMED GROUND TRUTH (.docs/integration/17-measmerize.md, .docs/prd/pdp.md §10-11):
- Measmerize is a third-party sizing widget powering TWO surfaces: Find My Size (body-measurement → size recommendation, updates CTA to "Recommended: Size X") and the Size Guide overlay (Measmerize-first, Contentful fallback when no Measmerize data exists, cm/inch toggle lives in the Contentful fallback only). Both point to the same underlying widget.
- INTEGRATION MODE CONFIRMED (2026-07-06): "Modal Integration" is the required path — the PWA owns the modal/slide-out shell (width, styling, tab switching between Measmerize and the Contentful fallback); Measmerize is inserted via `window.measmerize.modal.mount()` into `<div id="measmerize-modal">` (not an iframe). No `#measmerize-button` div is used. This is unusually well-specified compared to most tickets in this batch — script injection timing (once, on first mount, deferred behind LCP), SPA navigation handling (`window.measmerize.script.productCode = 'NEW_SKU'`), a full custom-event contract (`measmerize.widget.ready` / `.unavailable` / `.recommend` with `event.detail.defaultSize` / `.addToCart`), and defined failure-mode fallbacks are all already documented — say so as a genuine positive finding, not just problems.
- PDP PRD §10 confirms PRD-051/052 are explicitly "removed as not applicable for SFCC" — the Measmerize widget itself owns recommendation-click navigation and Find-My-Size-link suppression; SFCC/PWA does not build that logic. This meaningfully narrows what SFCC-101 actually needs to build (container/DOM/event wiring, not custom recommendation UI).
- ONE GENUINE, NAMED, STILL-OPEN BLOCKING DECISION: consent-gating approach (integration doc §7, item 1) — Zimmermann Privacy/Legal must confirm whether to (a) load the script freely and disable non-essential tracking via the SDK when consent is denied, or (b) gate the entire script load behind a Didomi consent category. Explicitly marked "blocking," owner Zimmermann, not resolved as of the doc's last state. This is the one real blocker here — separate from implementation readiness, which is otherwise strong.
- SCOPE QUESTION worth resolving from the ticket itself: the title says "Measmerize Widget & Find My Size CTA" — does NOT explicitly mention "Size Guide," even though the PRD treats Find My Size and Size Guide as two faces of the same widget/shell. Confirm whether Size Guide is in this ticket's scope, out of scope with its own separate ticket, or a gap nobody's written yet.
- POSSIBLE DE-RISK: SFCC-736 "pdp/drawer" (separate ticket, already merged as PR #67, "Ready for QA") built PDP slide-out tabs recently — check whether it already provides a reusable slide-out shell this ticket could plug Measmerize into, which would be a substantial scope reduction.

## One-line summary
A single reusable right-anchored drawer component with two content variants — a country-mismatch prompt (for SFCC-823) and an EU language-mismatch prompt (for SFCC-689) — purely presentational, with no trigger/redirect/cookie logic of its own.

1. **FE impact?** Yes — 100% frontend. No backend change is owned by this ticket.
2. **Clear enough to size?** Mostly. <result>## SFCC-277 — Cart Empty Cart State: Component Render Order & Logic

**One-line summary:** SFCC-277 defines a fixed 4-part stack (drawer header → Client Services text → Recommended For You → Zimmermann Benefits) and its trigger condition for the *cart drawer's* empty state; the render order itself is clear and matches an attached screenshot, but several dev-raised content/scope questions from early August were never confirmed before the ticket was PO-approved on 1 Sep.

Status: **Tech design**. Parent epic: SFCC-11 "Cart" (To Do, High priority). Assignee: Marcel Angelo Navarro. Labels: `CAI-012`, `Custom`, `Squad-A`.

---

### Seven-point sizing lens

1. **FE impact?** Yes — pure PWA Kit/Chakra assembly work inside the cart drawer, labelled Squad-A, traces to PRD `.docs/prd/cart.md` §2, CAI-012 ("Empty cart message shown when cart is empty").
2. **Clear enough to size?** Partially. The 4-item render order is unambiguous and matches the attached screenshot exactly. But: no formal Acceptance Criteria list is visible anywhere on the ticket (checked the description and a `fields=*all` fetch) despite Isabel Chaloner's 3 Aug comment explicitly referencing "AC6" — it likely lives in an unlinked Confluence TSD I couldn't locate. And 2 of her 3 questions only got a "likely" steer from Tim Lavelle, never a confirmed final answer, before PO approval.
3. **Which surfaces?** Cart drawer (mini-cart overlay) only — the ticket repeatedly says "within the cart drawer." Flag: it's labelled CAI-012, which in the PRD sits under **§2 Cart Page**, not §1 Mini-Cart — a scope mismatch worth confirming (see questions).
4. **Design/Figma dependencies?** Yes. See Design status below.
5. **API/backend dependencies?** Minimal for the trigger itself (basket item-count off the existing `useCurrentBasket` hook). Real dependency is Contentful for 2 of 4 stack items (SFCC-306 Client Services text — unassigned, still "To Do"; SFCC-316/317 Zimmermann Benefits — both "Tech design"). Recommended For You (SFCC-815) is already "Ready For Review" in Jira, which is notable since cart.md §12 (CAI-005) still logs the recommendation-engine platform (Einstein vs Athos Commerce) as unconfirmed.
6. **Pure FE / shared / architecture?** Pure FE + Contentful composition. No integration-team or architecture input needed beyond closing the two open content-ownership questions.
7. **Size now or need clarification?** The assembly/sequencing scope sizes now. Recommend not calling it "Ready" until the AC6 location, the heading content-source question, and the drawer-vs-full-page scope question are actually closed.

### Four axes

- **Behaviour:** Trigger is "the basket contains no items" — a plain 0-line-item check (PRD has no separate "saved for later" concept; only auth-gated Move-to-Wishlist exists). Unclear: does this need to handle a *live* transition (last item removed while the drawer is already open), and can a page-level notification (SFCC-404, listed only in the Populated sibling) ever need to coexist with the empty state (e.g. "item removed, now out of stock")? Neither ticket addresses this.
- **Desktop/mobile:** Not addressed at all — no breakpoint-specific behaviour is mentioned, unlike sibling SFCC-825 which spells out a fully different desktop (sticky/split-scroll) vs mobile (single continuous scroll) structure. The one screenshot appears to be a single viewport; whether the stack is identical on mobile is an assumption, not a stated fact.
- **A11y:** Not addressed at all. No heading level or focus-management contract for "YOUR BAG IS EMPTY" when the drawer opens directly into this state. Given AGENTS.md's WCAG 2.2 AA target and this almost certainly being a portal-rendered Chakra Drawer, this needs an explicit contract before build.
- **Data:** Contentful (Client Services text + Zimmermann Benefits) has a fallback behaviour — "don't render, empty string" — but it's only documented in Tim's comment reply, not written into the ticket as a formal AC. Recommended For You's signal for a shopper with *zero* cart context (browsing history? bestsellers?) isn't specified anywhere.

### Design status + source

A design exists specifically for this screen: attached screenshot `image-20260804-004155.png` (viewed directly) plus a Figma link marked **"Figma is leading"** (node-id 4905-9719, file "Zimmermann_Designs"). The screenshot confirms all 4 stack items, a 3-product Recommended For You carousel, a 3-icon Zimmermann Benefits band — and confirms there is **no "Continue Shopping" CTA anywhere in the design**; the only way out appears to be the drawer's close (X) icon or the dimmed nav visible behind it.

However, both centralized design-governance trackers, re-checked live (not from memory) just now, still show Cart as **not** signed off:
- **04.2 Design Tracker** (Confluence 258801666): Cart's "Mini-Cart" row (explicitly lists "empty cart state" as in scope) and "Full Cart Page" row are both **Design Status: PENDING / Zimmermann Sign-off: PENDING** — unchanged from a 13-Jul snapshot; the row's feedback notes haven't moved since 1 Jul, despite this ticket's screenshot (4 Aug) and PO approval (1 Sep) happening well after.
- **04.7 Component Inventory** (Confluence 400195591): the **Drawer** row — the literal shared container both SFCC-277 and SFCC-825 build inside — shows **"Designs Empty" / Status: Incomplete**.

So there's a real, current gap between ticket-level artefacts + PO approval and the trackers' recorded sign-off state. Could be the trackers are simply stale for Cart rather than a true block — the data doesn't tell me which — so this is a question, not a verdict.

### Empty/Populated split verdict: **Legitimate, with one flagged coordination gap**

- The two states are structurally very different, confirmed by comparing both attached screenshots directly: Populated has item-count-conditional scroll behaviour (≤3 vs >3 items), a sticky RHS summary, multiple payment/promo/tax UI, and documented desktop-vs-mobile divergence; Empty is a single-column, non-scrolling, non-transactional stack. This tracks the team's own "slice by data source, split again where risk/readiness differs" heuristic (Confluence 04.71 / decomposition pattern) — a real complexity boundary, not a cosmetic section cut.
- Both are independently demoable verticals, and SFCC-825's description explicitly calls itself "the populated cart equivalent of the empty cart state logic story (SFCC-277)" — a deliberate, acknowledged pairing.
- Good counter-evidence the team isn't mechanically splitting-by-state everywhere: **SFCC-301** "Cart Page – Recommendation Component Slot (**Empty and Populated Cart**)" is one ticket covering both states for that one slot, because that slot's behaviour doesn't differ by state. Splitting 277/825 but not 301 shows judgement, not a rote rule.
- **Flagged gap:** both tickets list **SFCC-315 (Cart Drawer Container)** as their first render-order item. Neither states which ticket owns building the actual top-level `isEmpty ? … : …` branch inside that shared shell — a real sequencing question the split doesn't resolve on its own.
- **Verified documentation gap (not a hypothesis):** SFCC-825's written render order **omits "Recommended For You" entirely**, yet its own attached screenshot clearly shows a 3-product "RECOMMENDED FOR YOU" carousel in the RHS sidebar — and SFCC-301's title confirms the slot belongs in both states. Worth fixing in SFCC-825's description regardless of the split verdict.

### Questions to raise

**BA** (Isabel Chaloner / ticket owner):
1. Where does the formal AC list live — the one referenced as "AC6"? Not in the description or any field I could read via the Jira API.
2. Isabel's two open questions (Contentful story needed for Client Services text? Is "YOUR BAG IS EMPTY" hardcoded or Contentful-managed?) only got a "likely" answer, never confirmed — close this out before sprint planning?
3. SFCC-277 is labelled CAI-012 (PRD §2 Cart Page) but scopes itself to "the cart drawer" (PRD §1 Mini-Cart). Does the standalone Cart Page need its own empty-state story, or does this one cover both surfaces?
4. Should the Contentful fetch-failure fallback (currently only in a comment reply) be added to the ticket as a formal AC?
5. Should SFCC-825's description be corrected to include Recommended For You (SFCC-301/SFCC-815), given the screenshot already shows it?

**Designer/UX:**
6. Does the empty-cart stack change at all between desktop and mobile/tablet, unlike its Populated sibling?
7. Is the missing "Continue Shopping" CTA deliberate, or an omission from this design pass?
8. Can the 04.2/04.7 trackers be updated to reflect current reality for Cart/Drawer (or confirm they're accurate)?

**Dev:**
9. Which of SFCC-277 / SFCC-825 owns building the top-level empty-vs-populated branch inside the shared SFCC-315 Drawer Container?
10. What heading level and focus-management behaviour should the empty-cart heading get, per WCAG 2.2 AA?
11. Does the empty state need to handle a live populated→empty transition, or is it only evaluated at drawer-open time?

**BA/Product:**
12. Has the CAI-005 recommendation-engine platform decision actually been finalized, given SFCC-815 is already Ready For Review? What signal does the empty-state carousel use with zero basket context?

### Readiness call

Sizeable at a high level today — the stack and its order are unambiguous and match a real design screenshot — but not sprint-ready: close the AC6/heading-source/scope-boundary questions with the BA and confirm SFCC-315 build ownership against SFCC-825 before committing.

---

**Couldn't check:** the live Figma file itself (relied on the one exported screenshot per ticket, since "Figma is leading" but no live Figma session was available in this environment — can't confirm later states/CTAs were added since 4 Aug); a Story Points/estimate field (none visible in the fields the Jira MCP tool surfaced); the true last-edited timestamp of either Confluence tracker (API returned blank `created`/`updated`, so I used the notes' own dates as a freshness proxy instead); Trello (no connector exists, and nothing in this ticket referenced it anyway).</result>

Badge is called for in SFCC-236's own AC but has zero implementation, and there's an unreconciled contradiction on whether it belongs on Homepage at all — which is correct, and when is it landing? — **SFCC-236 developer directly** (only the person mid-build on `feature/SFCC-236_product-card-shared-component` can answer what's actually left vs. deliberately deferred)

8. Confirm heading level for the section title and list semantics for the card row. — **Dev**
9. How should two same-page Group instances differentiate an identical visible link label for assistive tech? — **Dev**

**Readiness call:** Blocked on SFCC-236, which looks close — not a generic "blocked," but specifically: the dependency's 3-variation build is structurally complete and hardened, just sitting uncommitted with two explicitly-deferred (not silently missed) gaps, so size SFCC-743 now but hold the sprint commitment until SFCC-236 actually merges.</result>

<result>## SFCC-197 "Product Image Management" — Backlog Refinement Notes

**One-line summary:** This is a Merchandiser/BM-configuration and MuleSoft-mapping story that defines an "image view type" taxonomy (10 types) so uploaded product images get correctly tagged, ordered, and routed to the right storefront slot — it is *not* itself a PDP-gallery-build ticket, and the single biggest thing blocking a size is that the MuleSoft naming-convention-to-view-type mapping table is 100% unconfirmed.

Sources fetched: Jira `SFCC-197` (full issue, 20 comments, issuelinks, parent), Confluence page 400195591 ("04.7 Component Inventory," v13, live), Confluence page 450068481 ("04.4.5 Product Images — View Types & MuleSoft Mapping Rules," v4), plus repo checks of `overrides/app/components/image-gallery/`, `CODEOWNERS`, and the in-flight `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmProductCard/` (SFCC-236).

### Seven-point sizing lens

1. **Any FE impact?** Indirect/consumption-only. SFCC-197's real output is the *data contract* — a view-type tag per image — that FE components elsewhere (PDP gallery, PLP/card hover image, swatch selector, Shop-the-Look large/small) will consume.

See scope-ambiguity resolution below.
4. **Design/Figma dependencies?** Not for SFCC-197 itself (it has no UI). Relevant context for the coupled tickets — see Design status section below.
5. **API/backend dependencies?** Central and currently the largest gap: this ticket *is* the BM/MuleSoft integration story. See Data axis below.
6. **Pure FE / shared / architecture input?** Shared BM-config + MuleSoft-integration work with a downstream FE data-contract consequence. ### Four axes

- **Behaviour:** Well-defined at the taxonomy level; unevenly formalized as AC (Campaign/Runway/Product Styling now have explicit Given/When/Then; Flat Item/Detail/Model/Hidden/Front/Side/Back View don't yet).

- **Data (image asset source/CDN):** Ingestion path is clear (Studio → shared folder → MuleSoft → SFCC, alongside the AP21 product feed). What's *not* clear: the actual naming-convention-to-view-type mapping table in Confluence 450068481 has **every single row's pattern column literally marked "TBD"** — nothing is mapped yet. Also open in that same doc: front/side/back-view position numbers ("expected 3/4/5? TBD"), and a whole unresolved sub-question on whether position-based numbering even applies the same way to accessories vs. clothing (flagged as "cannot be confirmed until MuleSoft team is engaged"). Two separate tracking systems, not interchangeable:

- **PRD (`.docs/prd/pdp.md` §14):** PRD-065/066/068/069/070 are "ready for sign off" — a *business/product* confirmation status, not yet final.

  - "PDP Hero" (module) — status label "Done, minor update required" (confirmed by Dennis)
  - ↳ "Image Gallery" (sub-component) — status label "Done, minor update required" — **no "(confirmed by Dennis)" annotation on this specific row**, unlike its parent
  - ↳ "Product Content" (sub-component) — same "Done, minor update required," also unannotated
  - "Product Card Base" / "Image Carousel" / "Wishlist Icon" (i.e., the SFCC-236 card family) — all "Done" (confirmed by Dennis) — fully signed off, unlike the PDP Hero/Image Gallery side
  - Template "PDP" — Done (confirmed by Dennis), with an explicit note: "minor updates needed for PDP Hero and Product Cards Group"
  - **No tracked row exists for either "Shop the Look" component** (small/large) that today's AC update and Dani Rivett's 2026-09-01 comment depend on — a real design-tracker gap worth chasing.

Neither system says "fully confirmed" for the imagery-adjacent surfaces — they carry different caveats (business sign-off vs. design polish).

---

### Scope-ambiguity resolution

Per the actual ticket body and its issue links, this is **option (c) — BM/admin-config-flavored, with cross-surface FE consumption implications** — not a PDP-gallery-build ticket and not itself an overlap with the card-level SFCC-236 work in a code sense:

- The description is 100% about categorizing images in Business Manager via view types and how MuleSoft maps/orders them — no gallery/lightbox/zoom/component language anywhere in it.
- It **relates to** `SFCC-186` "PDP – Product Image Gallery" (Tech design, To Do) — that is the actual PDP-gallery FE-build ticket; SFCC-197 feeds it data, doesn't duplicate it.
- It explicitly **excludes video** to `SFCC-188`/`SFCC-302` (both Blocked).
- Real (data-only) touchpoint with SFCC-236: the "Model Image" view type is explicitly described as "a way to tag... an image as relevant to show on hover — e.g. it will show on a product card's hover state on PLP." That's a data-wiring dependency to flag for whoever integrates real product data into the card, not a scope clash with SFCC-197 or SFCC-236's own build.

---

### Vimeo / video-platform open item

Flagged directly, but **out of scope for SFCC-197**: the ticket's own description routes all video to `SFCC-188` ("PDP – Product Video in Gallery") and `SFCC-302` ("Product Video Management – BM Configuration"), both currently status Blocked. The PRD-067 Vimeo-unconfirmed-vs-Third-Party-Integrations-sheet conflict is real, per prior confirmed ground truth, but it's a dependency for those two sibling tickets, not a blocker for sizing SFCC-197.

### image-gallery Tier 2 / SFCC-bridge-pattern flag

Confirmed current state: `overrides/app/components/image-gallery/` **does not exist** — still un-overridden (base SFCC component), consistent with prior findings. `CODEOWNERS` already carries a forward-looking entry (`@ZimmermannAU/pwa-squad-b @ZimmermannAU/tier-2-approvers @ZimmermannAU/tier-1-approvers`) per `protectedFiles.md`'s "listed forward-lookingly, not descriptively" note. Grep confirms base SFCC's `image-gallery` is consumed internally only by `product-view/index.jsx` and `product-view-modal/bundle.jsx` (PDP-only, not `product-tile`) — confirming it's a genuine "SFCC bridge pattern" component per `overrideStyling.md`. **This flag isn't triggered by SFCC-197 itself** (no UI work here) but is directly relevant to sizing its sibling `SFCC-186`, where any future override would need a faithful, undecorated default export with brand styling in a theme recipe, not a decorated default.

---

### Specific questions to raise

1. **BA (Jasmijn/PO):** Is the AC now complete as of today's comment, or do Flat Item/Detail/Model/Hidden/Front/Side/Back View still need formal Given/When/Then blocks like Campaign/Runway/Product Styling just got?
2. **Integration lead / MuleSoft team (via BA):** When is the MuleSoft workshop, and can the naming-convention-to-view-type mapping table (currently all "TBD" in Confluence 450068481) be locked before this is called Ready — or is it acceptable to size with that as a parallel-track risk?
3. **BA + Design (Dennis):** Is there a tracked Figma status for the two Shop-the-Look components (small/large)? No row exists in the live 04.7 tracker.
4. **BA/PM (reconcile with SFCC-31 owner):** Does PRD-070's "required before publish" alt-text rule need an actual BM publish-blocking validation, given the documented mechanism always produces a fallback value and therefore has no "missing" state? Does SFCC-31 already cover this, or is there a gap?
5. **Dev/FE (atomic):** For the "Hidden" view type, does the MuleSoft feed still deliver hidden-tagged images to the storefront (for PLP/home rollover) while FE suppresses them only from the PDP gallery, or are they filtered upstream? Determines whether FE needs its own view-type filter logic.
6. **Dev/FE (atomic):** Does the legacy M2 position numbering in Jasmijn's 2026-08-24 comment (#1 base, #2 model, #3 styling, #6 swatch) carry over into the new SFCC view-type scheme, or is the Confluence doc's separate (also-TBD) position-3/4/5 = front/side/back proposal the one to build against?
7. **Integration lead (via BA):** Track the accessories-vs-clothing conditional-logic question as its own explicit open dependency — the mapping doc says it can't even be assessed for feasibility until MuleSoft is engaged.

### One-line readiness call

**Not Ready for sizing yet** — the hard architectural blocker is cleared (SFCC-800 spike Done), but AC is incomplete, the core MuleSoft mapping table is entirely unconfirmed, and two dependent components have no tracked design status; send back for one more grooming/MuleSoft-alignment pass rather than committing this sprint.</result>
